messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- The section never calls sdk.call, except "Vera.Ask.text" as said below: what the phone does is not its job.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them.
- If the section cannot really do it with this language and these components -- it needs a camera, a live feed, the person's location or data the phone does not hold -- decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it with made-up data.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

<classes>
</classes>
<fields>
</fields>
<functions>
function c_morning(state: AppState): number {
  let n: number = 0;
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) {
    if (e.minute < 720) { n = n + 1; }
  }
  return n;
}

function c_afternoon(state: AppState): number {
  let n: number = 0;
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) {
    if (e.minute >= 720 && e.minute < 1080) { n = n + 1; }
  }
  return n;
}

function c_evening(state: AppState): number {
  let n: number = 0;
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) {
    if (e.minute >= 1080) { n = n + 1; }
  }
  return n;
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let c_total: number = state.entries.length();
  if (c_total === 0) {
    sections.push(ui.Section("content", "", "", [ui.Text("caption", "Morning, afternoon and evening counts appear here once you log a headache.")]));
  } else {
    sections.push(ui.Section("content", "", "", [
      ui.SectionHeader("default", "By time of day", "When headaches start", ui.numberToString(c_total)),
      ui.MetricGroup("default", 3, [
        ui.NumberStat("default", "Morning", c_morning(state), "", "", 1, "before noon", "clock"),
        ui.NumberStat("default", "Afternoon", c_afternoon(state), "", "", 1, "noon to 6pm", "clock"),
        ui.NumberStat("default", "Evening", c_evening(state), "", "", 1, "6pm to midnight", "clock")
      ])
    ]));
  }
}
</view>

metadata.label: pickers-03
needs: A starter list of restaurant choices the person can pick from at random, such as pizza place, sushi bar, taco stand, burger joint, noodle house, and salad cafe. The person can add their own restaurants to the list and remove ones they don't want.

a scene the app draws itself: A spinning wheel drawn on screen with one slice per restaurant in the list. Tapping the wheel spins it; it slows and stops on one slice, and the restaurant on that slice is the pick, shown as the result. The person can spin again.

<classes>
</classes>
<fields>
c_word: string = ""
c_guesses: string[] = []
c_marks: string[] = []
c_input: string = ""
c_round: number = 0
c_message: string = ""
</fields>
<functions>
function c_pickWord(seed: number): string {
  let words: string[] = ["apple", "brave", "crane", "dwell", "eagle", "flame", "grape", "house", "ivory", "jolly", "knife", "lemon", "mango", "noble", "ocean", "piano", "queen", "river", "stone", "tiger", "unity", "vivid", "wheat", "youth", "zebra"];
  let n: number = words.length();
  let idx: number = math.randomBelow(seed, n);
  return words[idx];
}

function c_markGuess(word: string, guess: string): string {
  let result: string = "";
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < 5) {
    let g: string = strings.substring(guess, i, i + 1);
    let w: string = strings.substring(word, i, i + 1);
    if (g === w) {
      result = result + "c";
    } else {
      let found: boolean = false;
      let j: number = 0;
      while (j < 5) {
        let wj: string = strings.substring(word, j, j + 1);
        if (wj === g) {
          found = true;
        }
        j = j + 1;
      }
      if (found) {
        result = result + "p";
      } else {
        result = result + "a";
      }
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return result;
}

function c_start(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let seed: number = time.nowMillis() + state.c_round * 7919;
  let w: string = c_pickWord(seed);
  let empty: string[] = [];
  return {c_word: w, c_guesses: empty, c_marks: empty, c_input: "", c_round: state.c_round + 1, c_message: ""__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_setInput(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_input: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_submit(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (state.c_word === "") {
    return {c_message: "Start a round first."__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  if (state.c_guesses.length() >= 5) {
    return {c_message: "The round is over. Start a new round."__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let g: string = strings.toLowerCase(strings.trim(state.c_input));
  if (strings.length(g) !== 5) {
    return {c_message: "Enter a five-letter word."__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let mark: string = c_markGuess(state.c_word, g);
  let newGuesses: string[] = [];
  for (let old: string of state.c_guesses) {
    newGuesses.push(old);
  }
  newGuesses.push(g);
  let newMarks: string[] = [];
  for (let old: string of state.c_marks) {
    newMarks.push(old);
  }
  newMarks.push(mark);
  let msg: string = "";
  if (g === state.c_word) {
    msg = "You got it!";
  } else if (newGuesses.length() >= 5) {
    msg = "Out of tries. The word was " + state.c_word + ".";
  }
  return {c_guesses: newGuesses, c_marks: newMarks, c_input: "", c_message: msg__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
let c_over: boolean = state.c_guesses.length() >= 5 || (state.c_word !== "" && state.c_guesses.length() > 0 && state.c_guesses[state.c_guesses.length() - 1] === state.c_word);
let c_rows: ui.View[] = [];
let c_gi: number = 0;
while (c_gi < state.c_guesses.length()) {
  let c_g: string = state.c_guesses[c_gi];
  let c_m: string = state.c_marks[c_gi];
  let c_cells: ui.View[] = [];
  let c_li: number = 0;
  while (c_li < 5) {
    let c_letter: string = strings.toUpperCase(strings.substring(c_g, c_li, c_li + 1));
    let c_mk: string = strings.substring(c_m, c_li, c_li + 1);
    let c_style: string = "default";
    if (c_mk === "c") { c_style = "success"; }
    if (c_mk === "p") { c_style = "accent"; }
    if (c_mk === "a") { c_style = "danger"; }
    c_cells.push(ui.Cell(c_style, c_letter, "", 0, false));
    c_li = c_li + 1;
  }
  c_rows.push(ui.Grid("compact", 5, c_cells));
  c_gi = c_gi + 1;
}
let c_remaining: number = 5 - state.c_guesses.length();
let c_status: string = "";
if (state.c_word === "") {
  c_status = "Tap Start to begin a round.";
} else if (c_over) {
  c_status = "Round over. The word was " + strings.toUpperCase(state.c_word) + ".";
} else {
  c_status = ui.numberToString(c_remaining) + " tries left.";
}
sections.push(ui.Section("hero", "Round", c_status, [
  ui.When(state.c_word === "", ui.ActionBar("center", [
    ui.Button("primary", "Start round", "c_start", 0, true)
  ])),
  ui.When(state.c_word !== "" && !c_over, ui.Column("default", [
    ui.TextField("default", "Your guess", state.c_input, "c_setInput", "", true, "Enter a five-letter word.", 5, "Use exactly five letters.", 5, "Use exactly five letters."),
    ui.ActionBar("end", [
      ui.Button("primary", "Submit guess", "c_submit", 0, true)
    ])
  ])),
  ui.When(c_over, ui.ActionBar("center", [
    ui.Button("primary", "New round", "c_start", 0, true)
  ])),
  ui.When(state.c_message !== "", ui.Text("caption", state.c_message))
]));
sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Guesses", "", [
  ui.When(state.c_guesses.length() === 0, ui.EmptyState("default", "No guesses yet", "Type a five-letter word and submit it.", "", "", "list")),
  ui.When(state.c_guesses.length() > 0, ui.Column("default", c_rows))
]));
</view>

metadata.label: word-games-04
needs: A hidden five-letter word chosen by the app at the start of each round, kept secret until the round ends. The person types a five-letter guess and taps to submit it; the phone marks each letter of the guess as correct in the right place, present but in the wrong place, or absent, and shows the guesses so far with their marks. After five wrong guesses the round ends and the hidden word is revealed; a correct guess ends the round early. A button starts a new round with a fresh hidden word.
